_about: Dutch locale example. Common English (and a few other) words in Dutch text, spelled the way the Dutch AI voice says them as a Dutch speaker would. scripts/vo/pronounce.py applies this to the speech text before recording (gen.py, VO_LANG=nl). Why: 'Cube' and 'site' came out as Dutch words ('kuu-be', 'sie-te'), and the voice gate didn't see it because whisper writes them correctly. Whole words, case-insensitive. A brand or product name that sounds different goes into lines.json itself, in 'speech'. Dutch 'aj' before a consonant is heard as 'a' ('websajt' came out as 'websat'), so the sound 'ai' is written 'ai' (websait, onlain, laif). A lone 'site' at the end of a question became 'zet', 'zee' or 'set' with 'sait' and 'zaad' with 'sajt'; 'saait' gave 'site' 4 out of 4 times. Another language gets its own reference/lang/<lang>/pronunciation.json with the same shape.
_pause: A pause in the voice is made with a full stop, not a comma: the voice rests too briefly at a comma ('Kijk op onze site. Of app ons.').
_suffixes: Also at the end of a compound word (watertank -> watertenk, water-tank -> water-tenk).
